moat_source: etch/deposition process leadership and a large installed base feeding services revenue (record $2.1B CSBG quarter); evidence: 50%+ gross margin and +41% EPS growth, but the customer set is the most cyclical in semiconductors

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. Excludes dividend/buybacks.

primary_model_risk: Memory cycle timing: Lam's order book today is a function of Micron/Samsung/SK hynix responding to 85% DRAM gross margins with capacity. That same response is what cracks memory pricing - and memory tool orders - in 2027-2028. The base case models a mid-horizon digestion; if it arrives earlier or deeper (the historical norm after supercycles), the bear case governs.
expectations_gap_key_variable: memory-cycle permanence: at $349.64 (~53x forward EPS) the market prices the $140B WFE year as a plateau, not a peak; our base case includes the digestion year that has followed every memory capex boom on record
top_5_bull_arguments: Record revenue and EPS with a beat-and-raise cadence (+24% revenue, +41% EPS y/y)
The memory supercycle math: 85% DRAM margins force a multi-year capacity build that flows directly to Lam's order book
CY2026 WFE outlook raised to $140B with H2 stronger than H1
Services (CSBG) at a record $2.1B/quarter adds a recurring cushion absent in prior cycles
Balance sheet and capital returns are pristine (grade A across the board)
top_5_bear_arguments: Expected IV ($139.80) is ~60% below the price - compounder multiples on the most cyclical semicap franchise
The -13.87% week tracking Micron tick-for-tick shows the market already trades LRCX as a memory derivative
Every memory capex supercycle has been followed by an order collapse; 53x forward leaves zero room for that history
Regulatory High: China exposure in a tightening export-control regime
WFE outlooks revise down faster than up once memory spot prices turn
thesis_breakers: First DRAM/NAND price decline (leading indicator for tool-order deferrals)
Q4 FY2026 actuals below $6.2B (bottom of guide)
Memory customer capex cuts announced (Micron/Samsung/SK hynix)
CSBG revenue declining sequentially (the recurring cushion failing)
